basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 6.' and it opens 'Vers. 6. Abiit in alteram regionem. Hic quaeri potest cur Esau post mortem patris dicatur'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 6. Abiit in alteram regionem. Hic quaeri potest cur Esau post mortem patris dicatur abiisse in Seir, et recessisse a fratre suo, cum jam, quando venit Jacob, in Seir dicatur habitasse? Sed fieri potuit ut, Jacob fugiente in Mesopotamiam, dolore et ira praereptae sibi benedictionis recesserit a parentibus, et habitaverit in Seir per viginti annos, quibus Jacob absens fuit. Postquam vero reversus est Jacob, et fratri suo reconciliatur, rursus de Seir cum fratre suo, donec pater vixit, nabitavit cum eo. Isaac | mortuo, sicut hic dicitur, tulit substantiam domus suae et recessit a fratre suo. Divites enim erant valde, et simul habitare non poterant.
